intro.title: Build memory leak detection test run
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test run that simulates and detects a memory leak in a Node.js application. You will learn how to create a simple server that intentionally leaks memory by adding data to an array without cleaning it up. The core concept involves understanding how memory allocation works in Node.js and using built-in tools to monitor memory usage. You will work with JavaScript arrays, HTTP servers, and the global `process` object to track memory growth over time. This hands-on exercise will help you recognize common patterns that lead to memory leaks and how to test for them effectively.
intro.usecase: Memory leak detection is critical for long-running Node.js applications like monitoring dashboards, API gateways, and real-time analytics systems. Developers use these techniques to ensure production servers don't gradually consume all available memory, which would cause crashes in services like e-commerce platforms or financial transaction processors. By implementing leak detection tests, teams can proactively identify issues in microservices, background job processors, or WebSocket servers before they impact users. This pattern is especially valuable for applications requiring 24/7 uptime, such as healthcare monitoring systems or IoT data aggregation services.

objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with memory monitoring dependencies
Configure a test script to simulate memory-intensive operations
Implement a memory leak detection function using process.memoryUsage()
Construct a test runner that executes leak detection at intervals
Integrate console logging to display real-time memory consumption data
Manipulate object creation patterns to intentionally trigger memory leaks
Apply cleanup mechanisms to prevent memory accumulation in test scenarios

steps.title: Implement periodic memory checks
steps.instruction: Inside your detectMemoryLeak function, add a setInterval call that will run every 2 seconds to check current memory usage and compare it with the initial measurement.

steps.hint: You'll need to calculate the memory increase percentage and check if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 10%). If it does, set a flag variable to indicate a leak.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will include logic that calculates memory increase percentage and sets a leak flag when the threshold is exceeded.
successCriteria: Code includes comparison logic that calculates memory increase percentage and sets a leak flag variable when threshold is exceeded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the leak detection logic that compares memory usage and flags leaks when thresholds are exceeded.
